channel.title: Israel National News Flashes
channel.description: Latest news flashes from Israel National News

item.title: Likud attacks Lapid: His statement was prepared in advance, unrelated to the meeting
item.description:
The Likud party criticized opposition leader Yair Lapid after the Prime Minister’s Office issued a statement following his meeting with Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu. The party claimed that Lapid issued a political statement attacking Netanyahu just minutes after the meeting ended.
“He left the meeting with Prime Minister Netanyahu at 11:39 p.m. At 11:41 p.m., just two minutes later, at record speed, he issued a lengthy statement that was entirely a political attack on the Prime Minister," Likud said. “Either he writes at the speed of light, or the statement was prepared in advance and had nothing to do with the briefing he received. So much for the late-night Lapid."

item.title: PMO: Lapid was briefed on warnings of possible attacks ahead of the elections
item.description:
Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu concluded a security briefing with opposition leader Yair Lapid, attended by the Prime Minister’s military secretary and the Military Secretariat’s intelligence officer.
The Prime Minister’s Office said the intelligence briefing included detailed warnings of possible attacks on various fronts ahead of the elections.

item.title: 13-year-old from Qalandiya arrested on suspicion of arson near Kokhav Yaakov
item.description:
Police launched an investigation into suspected arson in an open area near the community of Kokhav Yaakov. IDF soldiers from the Binyamin Brigade who were called to the scene arrested a suspect in connection with the incident.
The suspect, a 13-year-old resident of Qalandiya, was taken for questioning at the Binyamin police station. The investigation is ongoing.

item.title: Stop asking why they hate us. Love being a Jew.
item.description: The blessing of being Jewish in this world is to live every stage of life with dignity, meaning, and purpose. Op-ed.

item.title: Lapid after security briefing with Netanyahu: No reason to cause public panic
item.description:
Opposition leader Yair Lapid commented on the security briefing he received from Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, saying he would not violate the confidentiality of the briefing, but argued that “Israel’s security and IDF bases are not the backdrop for campaign videos."
According to Lapid, the IDF, Shin Bet and police are prepared for the elections and “there is no reason to cause public panic." He added that he demanded Netanyahu hold a meeting with the Shin Bet chief and Central Elections Committee Chairman Justice Noam Solberg ahead of the election.

item.title: Sukkah Fortress
item.description: The strength required to build our home, that is, our national homeland, must be spiritual might, the might of the festival, the might of God’s eternal word.

item.title: Trump: Iran is doing very poorly and will eventually give up
item.description: President Trump says Iran is struggling and will eventually “give up," while insisting Tehran cannot be allowed to obtain a nuclear weapon.

item.title: Mother of terror attack victim Neria Leiter: 'A time of uncertainty'
item.description: Nearly a week after Neria Leiter was critically wounded in a terror attack on Route 443, his mother, Hani, speaks about the uncertainty in the ICU, hopes for his recovery, and the family that has remained by his side around the clock.

item.description: Anti-Defamation League criticizes New York City mayor's newly unveiled strategy to combat antisemitism, citing lack of formal definition and accusing him of prioritizing his 'anti-Israel agenda.'

item.title: Yigal Amir requested leave to visit his sick father and was denied
item.description: Larissa Amir Trimbobler attacked National Security Minister Itamar Ben-Gvir after Yigal Amir’s request for special leave due to his 85-year-old father’s condition was denied on security issues.

item.title: Hamas’ enemy turns partner: Dahlan-Hamas rapprochement signals battle for post-Abbas era
item.description: For years, Mohammed Dahlan was one of Hamas’s fiercest enemies and a senior figure in the Palestinian security services that fought the organization. Now, a dramatic rapprochement causes worry on the battle over who will succeed Mahmoud Abbas.

item.title: Rabbi Kenneth Brander: ‘There is nothing Jewish about terrorizing innocent people'
item.description: Ohr Torah Stone President Rabbi Dr. Kenneth Brander condemns the attack on Jalud, calling for those responsible to be investigated and held accountable.

item.title: Antisemitism or political sabotage? Past quotes stir controversy in France
item.description: Mediapart published conversations from 2013 in which antisemitic statements are attributed to the president of the right-wing party. Bardella denies the allegations and has filed a defamation lawsuit.

item.title: Innocent? Death row inmate released from prison after 41 years
item.description: A man who spent 41 years on death row in the US after being convicted of killing a woman has been released on bail after prosecutors said a new analysis of DNA evidence did not link him to the crime.

item.title: Morocco makes history: King appoints first female prime minister
item.description: King Mohammed VI has appointed Fatima Ezzahra El Mansouri as Morocco’s prime minister after her party won the largest number of seats in the parliamentary elections.

item.title: “False blood libels": Netanyahu launches legal battle against media
item.description: Prime Minister files NIS 2.6 million defamation lawsuit against media outlets and journalists over reports that he received warnings before October 7.

item.title: Ireland won a game of Football 3-0. It lost everything else
item.description: Ireland can keep the three points, it must also own the ugliness it brought into the “Beautiful Game."

item.title: Reporters came to cover an accident, witnessed another accident
item.description: A TVP Info crew covering a fatal accident in Poland captured another crash as a car hit a 14-year-old girl on a scooter. The reporter and cameraman rushed to help.

item.title: Islamic preacher in Melbourne calls for taking up arms against Jews and Christians
item.description: Melbourne Islamic preacher calls in a sermon to reject Jews and Christians as friends and take up arms against them, amid criticism over Australia's response to extremist incitement.

item.title: Frankly my dear, I don’t give a damn
item.description: Antisemitism is so hip, so cool. Don’t these people know that they have moved to the side of the devil? Opinion.

item.title: Dramatic rescue: Paramedic climbs 55 meters to rescue construction worker
item.description: A construction worker lost consciousness in a crane cab in Kiryat Bialik. An MDA paramedic climbed 55 meters to treat him and he was evacuated to Rambam in stable condition.

item.title: “Our enemies will try to attack us": Lapid demands clarification from Netanyahu on threat
item.description: Netanyahu said there are indications that Israel’s enemies will attempt to attack ahead of the elections. Lapid demanded an urgent briefing, and Netanyahu instructed his military secretary to update him.

item.title: Smotrich orders preparations for additional fuel subsidies amid energy crisis
item.description: The Finance Minister instructed professional officials to prepare for additional subsidies on gasoline prices, in an effort to mitigate the expected increase amid the global energy crisis.

item.title: Yair Golan demands: 'Disqualify Otzma Yehudit'
item.description: After their request was rejected by the Central Elections Committee, the Democrats party petitioned the Supreme Court, demanding that Otzma Yehudit be disqualified from running for the Knesset.

item.title: Defense Minister threatens Hamas leaders abroad
item.description: Minister Katz responded to the elimination of the commander of Hamas' Northern Gaza Brigade and made clear that the defense establishment will continue pursuing the terrorist organization's senior leaders.

item.title: KKL-JNF clarifies: No parties will be held at Nova site
item.description: Ahead of the anniversary of October 7, KKL-JNF clarified that visits to the Nova site in the Re’im Forest will be permitted solely for remembrance and commemoration.

item.description: Israeli defense company UVision is partnering with Estonia’s LendurAI to integrate advanced AI and autonomous capabilities into its loitering munitions for an undisclosed NATO member state.
